# refactor(domain): assign error ownership by meaning

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

Lands after the issue that splits config I/O from config policy, and builds on it.

## What

Every kind of failure jig reports has a clear owner. Users see the same error messages, and the
same failures are retried, blocked or fatal.

## Why

All failures live in one domain file, together with error helpers and retry execution. Business
code therefore appears to depend on storage, Git and configuration details, and each new failure
type adds to a single global list.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec section: "Error ownership and technical failure handling".

- `src/domain/errors.ts` (220 lines) holds the `JigError` union, `FailureKind`, `isTransient`,
  `isJigError`, `messageOf`, `rootCause` and 21 error classes: `AgentRunFailed`,
  `AgentOutputInvalid`, `PlanNotCovered`, `DesignUnresolved`, `RemoteUnavailable`,
  `SandboxUnavailable`, `SetupCommandFailed`, `RunStateConflict`, `RunCodeUnavailable`,
  `MergeFailed`, `GitCommandFailed`, `CommitImportRefused`, `CommitRejected`, `ConfigInvalid`,
  `RunRequestInvalid`, `RunInProgress`, `MetricsLogCorrupt`, `LocalStateUnwritable`,
  `CodexLoginNotSaved`, `ImageBuildFailed`, `CommandInputInvalid`.
- `src/domain/retry.ts` combines the transient-error policy with retry execution.
- `src/integrations/github/errors.ts` holds GitHub-specific errors; leave them for the GitHub issue
  unless a shared class is involved.

Ownership:

- Domain keeps business failures, such as `PlanNotCovered` and `DesignUnresolved`.
- Ports own capability failures (storage, Git, sandbox), defined once, without raw library details.
- Config owns configuration-validation failures. **`ConfigInvalid` appears in `RunStoreFailure`
  (`src/ports/run-store.ts`)**: moving it into config unchanged would make ports depend on config.
  First list what it actually means at each use, then split it or define the portable contract
  below its consumers.
- CLI owns transport input failures (`CommandInputInvalid`). App owns use-case failures.
- Adapters translate raw third-party exceptions into the declared capability failures.

Before moving anything, list the consumers of each helper and separate four things: what an error
means, retry/block/fatal classification, presentation and unwrapping (`messageOf`, `rootCause`),
and retry execution. Use better-result facilities instead of rebuilding them. Keep a thin wrapper
only where it preserves behavior the library lacks, and say which behavior in the PR. Use narrow
unions where a decision is exhaustive. An aggregate union may live at the application boundary
that needs it; domain and flow must not import it. Flow's failure type comes from the steps and
stores it calls. Remove registry machinery that nothing uses instead of moving it.

Do not create a top-level `failures` or shared-utilities owner. If the inventory shows that one is
needed, stop and propose its responsibility, consumers and allowed dependency edges in the PR
description before building it.

## Done when

- [ ] The PR contains a table listing every error's old owner, new owner, and how its tag, fields
      and retry/block/fatal classification are preserved at its consumers.
- [ ] Domain imports no capability, config or CLI error. Ports import nothing outside domain and ports.
- [ ] No moved error creates an outward import or a cycle (`npm run lint:dependencies`).
- [ ] Behavior tests show unchanged classification and user-visible messages, including
      original-cause reporting.
- [ ] The verification below passes.

## Verification

From the repository root using the pinned Node version (`volta` in `package.json`):

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. In the PR, state which owner each
moved concept now belongs to and why.


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/56
